A few well-known masnoon duas with meaning and source. To confirm the Arabic text, check a reliable book such as Hisn al-Muslim.

1. On waking up

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِيْ أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُوْرُ

All praise is for Allah who gave us life after causing us to die (sleep), and to Him is the resurrection.

Source: Sahih al-Bukhari

2. Before sleeping

بِاسْمِكَ اللّٰهُمَّ أَمُوْتُ وَأَحْيَا

In Your name, O Allah, I die (sleep) and I live (wake).

Source: Sahih al-Bukhari

3. Leaving the house

بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللّٰهِ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ

In the name of Allah, I place my trust in Allah; there is no might or power except with Allah.

Source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami at-Tirmidhi

4. Before eating

بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ

In the name of Allah (I begin).

Source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami at-Tirmidhi

5. After eating

اَلْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهِ الَّذِيْ أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِيْنَ

All praise is for Allah who fed us, gave us drink and made us Muslims.

Source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami at-Tirmidhi

6. Entering the mosque

اَللّٰهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِيْ أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ

O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.

Source: Sahih Muslim

7. Leaving the mosque

اَللّٰهُمَّ إِنِّيْ أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ

O Allah, I ask You for Your bounty.

Source: Sahih Muslim

8. Dua for travel

سُبْحَانَ الَّذِيْ سَخَّرَ لَنَا هٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِيْنَ وَإِنَّا إِلٰى رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُوْنَ

Glory to Him who has subjected this to us, and we could not have subdued it ourselves; and to our Lord we shall surely return.

Source: Quran (Az-Zukhruf 13–14), Sahih Muslim

Well-known adhkar and Quranic supplications. Their virtue is only what the source states; please do not attribute more to them.

1. Dua in distress and worry

لَّا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا أَنتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ

There is no god but You, glory be to You; truly I have been among the wrongdoers.

Source: Quran (Al-Anbiya 87). A hadith in Tirmidhi says that when a Muslim makes this dua for anything, Allah answers it.

2. Hasbunallah

حَسْبُنَا اللّٰهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيْلُ

Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs.

Source: Quran (Aal Imran 173).

3. La hawla wa la quwwata

لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللّٰهِ

There is no might and no power except with Allah.

Source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim. A hadith calls it one of the treasures of Paradise.

How to use the tasbeeh counter

  1. Choose a target: 33, 99, 100 or free.
  2. Tap the big button each time you say the dhikr.
  3. When the target is reached the tool tells you and moves to the next dhikr by itself.
  4. For the after-prayer tasbeeh (SubhanAllah 33, Alhamdulillah 33, Allahu Akbar 34) choose a target of 33. For the third dhikr switch the target to “Free” to count up to 34.

Tasbeeh FAQ

How many times should I do tasbeeh?

There is no single limit. The after-prayer tasbeeh (33, 33 and 34) is reported in a hadith; other adhkar can be said as much as you are able.

Is my count saved?

Yes, in your phone's browser. It is erased if you clear the browser's data.

What if the keep-screen-awake button does not work?

This feature is not available in every browser. In that case, increase the screen timeout in your phone settings.

Are these duas authentic?

Each dua has its source written beside it. For peace of mind, confirm it in Hisn al-Muslim or with a scholar.
